answers.text: The reply puts the fixes in priority order and says what needs a person
answers.evidence: The final reply ranks its problems under 'Fix these before launch' (items 1–5), 'Fix next' (6–11) and 'Smaller issues', and its 'Suggested order' puts items 1, 2 and 5 first because they 'can create wrong or duplicate reservations at the desk, or lock members out'. It says 'I did not run the pages in a browser or on a phone, and I did not test them with a screen reader', and that the real-phone, dark-mode, VoiceOver and 200% text-size check 'is still to do'.

mapping.title: Closed days can be picked and are refused only at Confirm, with no way back
mapping.reason: A R1 and B R1 agree. Same as D06: any of the next 21 days can be picked, closed days included, and the refusal ('The library is closed on … Choose another day') comes only after the details are filled in and Confirm is tapped; 'That error has no link and no way to change the day', and the basket not letting the day be edited is part of the same no-way-back harm.

mapping.title: Days before the tool's 'Available from' date are not blocked
mapping.reason: A R2 and B R2 agree. Same as D14: days before 'Available from' are not blocked and the reservation 'succeeds' (the pressure washer, available from 17 Oct, reserved for Saturday 10 Oct; the ground truth's example is the wet tile saw), so the desk holds a reservation for a tool it does not have.

mapping.title: Pick-up date chosen twice, and the two can disagree
mapping.reason: A R3 and B R3 agree. Same as D15: the tool-page day and the basket session are not reconciled ('Nothing links the two'), so the confirm page shows 'pick up Saturday 17 October' above 'Pick-up session: Wednesday 21 October'; the closed-day check reading the tool-page day is a consequence of the same unreconciled dates. The item's main harm is the contradiction, so D15 rather than D23.

mapping.title: Ten-minute basket hold expires silently, then a misleading error and a lock-out
mapping.reason: A R4 and B R4 agree. Same as D10: the basket only says 'Items are held for you while you finish', with no time, warning or extension, and once the hold lapses Continue shows only 'Something went wrong. Try again.'; that retrying never works is part of how the lapsed hold is handled, and the proposed fix (state the limit, warn, say plainly that it expired) fixes D10.

mapping.title: Truncated names make the two drills look identical on a phone
mapping.reason: A R5 and B R5 agree. Same as D03: names are cut to one line with an ellipsis, so at 375 px both drills show as about 'Cordless drill 18 V, co…'.

mapping.title: On phones the results come before search, and the date filter is behind an icon-only button
mapping.reason: A R6 and B R6 agree. Same as D01: at 480 px and below 'the results come before the search form', and the 'Available from' filter 'sits behind an icon-only button below that'.

mapping.title: Desktop: form shown first but coded after the results
mapping.reason: A R7 and B R7 agree. Wrong as stated: the ground truth gives the document order as form then results, so on desktop, where the form is shown first, visual and keyboard/screen-reader order agree; the real mismatch is at 480 px and below, already counted under R6 (D01).

mapping.title: 330 px minimum column makes the page scroll sideways at 320 px and high zoom
mapping.reason: A R8 and B R8 agree. Same as D05: the results grid's 330 px minimum column width makes the page scroll sideways 'At 320 px wide, or at high zoom'.

mapping.title: A search with no results leaves the old list and shows no message
mapping.reason: A R9 and B R9 agree. Same as D02: search() 'only redraws when it finds something', so the previous list stays, with no 'No tools match' message and nothing announced to screen readers.

mapping.title: Double-tapping Confirm makes two reservations
mapping.reason: A R10 and B R10 agree. Same as D12: Confirm stays enabled through the 1.5 s wait with no visible busy state, and a second tap creates a second reservation number, so 'The desk sets the tool aside twice'.

mapping.title: Basket Continue button has no busy state
mapping.reason: A R11 and B R11 agree. Not in the ground truth and a different control from D12 ('The Continue button in the basket has the same missing busy state'): Continue waits about 1.2 s (D10 records the wait) with nothing showing it is working, so a member on a slow phone cannot tell the tap registered and may tap again or give up; minor.

mapping.title: Dark-mode 'Available from' badge fails contrast
mapping.reason: A R12 and B R12 agree. Same as D04: in dark mode the badge's #2f7d4a on #1d2622 is 3.07:1 for 16 px bold text against the 4.5:1 needed; the CSS not following DESIGN.md's #8fd1a8 is the cause and fix of the same failure. A also folded the badge-background remark into this item; it is R13 here (see settled).

mapping.title: Dark-mode badge background is the same colour as the card
mapping.reason: B R13; A had no separate item, having merged this remark into its R12 (see settled). 'The badge background is also the same colour as the card, so it doesn't look like a badge' is a styling remark: the legibility harm is the text contrast already mapped to D04 under R12, and no effect on members of the badge not looking like a badge is stated or evident.

mapping.title: Loan-length dropdown traps Tab and ignores Escape
mapping.reason: A R13 and B R14 agree. Same as D09: once the list is open, 'Tab and Shift+Tab only cycle through the options, Escape doesn't close it', so it can only be left by choosing an option; that tapping outside does not close it is the same can't-leave-the-list problem.

mapping.title: Loan-length button's accessible name is only 'One week'
mapping.reason: A R14 and B R15 agree. Same as D16: the button's accessible name is just its current value, 'One week', without 'Loan length', so a screen-reader user is not told what is being chosen.

mapping.title: 'Added to your basket' vanishes after about 1.2 s with no next step
mapping.reason: A R15 and B R16 agree. Feedback after the press, so D07: the message 'disappears after about 1.2 s', too fast for older members, and the small 'Basket (1)' header link is the only lasting way forward; the item does not claim the member believes the tool is already reserved, so not D26.

mapping.title: Basket sessions shown in reverse order
mapping.reason: A R16 and B R17 agree. Same as D11: row-reverse and wrap-reverse put Wed 28 Oct at the top on a phone, while 'Screen readers and keyboard users get them earliest first'.

mapping.title: Membership and phone checks too strict
mapping.reason: A R17 and B R18 agree. Same as D17: 'ft-01234', 'FT 01234', '+44 7700 900123' and '07700 900 123' are rejected because nothing normalises them before the strict patterns are applied.

mapping.title: 'Open' becomes an unlabelled 8 px dot on phones
mapping.reason: A R18 and B R19 agree. Same as D20: 'Below 480 px it becomes an unlabelled 8 px dot', so on a phone it is easy to miss which days are sessions.

mapping.title: Done page shows a made-up reservation number without reservation data
mapping.reason: A R19 and B R20 agree. Not in the ground truth: opened without reservation data (for example reopened later from history), the done page shows 'FT-4471' as though a reservation exists, a false confirmation a member could rely on or quote at the desk; an edge case, but misleading.

mapping.title: Reservation numbers share the 'FT-' prefix with membership numbers
mapping.reason: A R20 and B R21 agree. Not in the ground truth: reservation numbers (FT-4471) and membership numbers (FT-01234) share the 'FT-' prefix, so a member, many of them older, can give the wrong number at the desk or type a reservation number into the membership field; minor.

mapping.title: Basket not emptied after confirming
mapping.reason: A R21 and B R22 agree. Same as D18: after confirming, the basket still holds the tools unless the member taps 'Reserve another tool', so the same tool can be reserved again.

mapping.title: 'Up to three tools' limit not enforced
mapping.reason: A R22 and B R23 agree. Same as D21: the stated limit of three tools is not enforced, so a reservation can include more tools than the desk will lend.

mapping.title: Fixed Reserve bar covers the footer and desk phone number
mapping.reason: A R23 and B R24 agree. Same underlying problem as D08, stated more narrowly: nothing keeps the tool page clear of the fixed bar, so 'the footer, which has the desk phone number' sits under it at the bottom of the page, a case D08 names; it omits the focused day buttons hidden under the bar.

mapping.title: 'Choose a pick-up day first' is not announced; focus jumps to the first day
mapping.reason: A R24 and B R25 agree. Same as D19: when Reserve is tapped with no day chosen, the error 'isn't read out' and 'Focus moves to the first day button instead'.

mapping.title: Card tool names are h2 inside the 'Tools' h2
mapping.reason: A R25 (real-unseeded) and B R26 (not-a-problem) split; settled as not-a-problem (see settled). The review says only that tool names on cards are h2 inside the 'Tools' h2 and should be h3, and names no effect on members; every tool name is still a heading a screen-reader member can jump to and hear, so the level costs nothing in finding or reserving a tool. A markup tidy-up, not a barrier.

mapping.title: Done page reads the tool name twice (hidden #c-tool)
mapping.reason: A R26 and B R27 agree. Same as D24: on the done page 'the hidden #c-tool makes screen readers read the tool name twice'.

settled.a: no separate item: A merged the remark into its R12 (tool-library-D04)
settled.reason: Alignment decision: split, as B did. Item 6 of the report makes two claims. The contrast claim ('#2f7d4a on #1d2622. That's 3.07:1, and 16 px bold text needs 4.5:1', with DESIGN.md's #8fd1a8 as its cause and fix) is D04 and stays R12, as both graders mapped it. The next sentence, 'The badge background is also the same colour as the card, so it doesn't look like a badge', is a different problem: it concerns the badge's fill rather than its text colour, it has a different consequence (the badge does not look like a badge, rather than being hard to read), and it needs a different fix, because switching the text to #8fd1a8 fixes D04 and leaves the background as it is. The mapping instructions count 'two different problems in one paragraph' as two items. Both graders also split this review's other sentences that add a separate deficiency to a numbered item (the basket Continue's missing busy state in item 5, the loan-length name in item 7, the 'FT-' prefix in the smaller issues), and merged only sub-points that share the main point's harm (the basket not letting the day be edited, the closed-day check reading the tool-page day, tapping outside the loan-length list). A's reason, that the remark 'describes the same dark-theme styling of this badge', groups by element and theme, not by problem. Judged on what it says, the remark states no effect on members, and none is evident beyond the legibility already mapped to D04, so B's not-a-problem. After this split the consensus numbering follows B's from R13 on: consensus R14–R27 are A's R13–R26.

Mapping decision. The review's whole item is that tool names on cards are h2 inside the 'Tools' h2 and should be made h3; it names no effect on members. real-unseeded needs a genuine problem for these members and a reason it would hurt them. A's reason, that a screen-reader member navigating by headings 'gets a flat outline in which the tools do not sit under that section (WCAG 1.3.1)', restates the markup without naming anything a member cannot do or does more slowly. Every tool name is still a heading, so a screen-reader member can still jump from tool to tool and hear each name, and nothing is hidden, unlabelled or read out of order. With no harm shown or evident it is a markup tidy-up: not-a-problem, as B judged.
